blind.why: Shaded-alley smoke (CS2 t4_017) vs ours on Long at 16 m t=10 s (long_t10). CS2's smoke takes on the scene light: cool grey in shade, wispy, fading into the ground. Ours is a glowing near-white cotton dome with a flat, ragged bottom line. It is brighter than the sunlit sandstone around it and looks pasted on.

Sunlit site smoke (t4_030) vs ours at B Site from B Door, 18 m, t=8.5 s (bsite_t8p5). CS2's smoke is dust-toned, with a lit side and a shaded side and a billowing, irregular silhouette. Ours is a stack of pure-white round lobes with almost no shading and no warm tint.

Close smoke in an enclosed space (t4_031) vs ours in Lower Tunnel 2.5 m from the front of the cloud (tun_t1). Ours shows a flat grey wall with vertical banding seams between puffs, dark smudge blotches along the edges, and a hard scalloped top against the dark roof. It also glows much brighter than the dim tunnel.

Aim preview (preview_static_strong_long) vs CS2's trajectory line (t4_015). CS2's line is one thin, continuous, readable curve. Ours is a fat cyan hook near the crosshair plus scattered dots and a faint far segment, so it is hard to read where the grenade will land.

biggest_gap: Haze still reads as an overbright white cotton-wool impostor, not smoke lit by the scene. Repro: test=1&seed=1; debug.spawn('haze',{x:38,y:.07,z:14}); place(38,0,30,yaw 0); advance 10 (long_t10.png). Also spawn at B Site (-33,-31) and view from B Door (-19,-43) (bsite_t8p5.png). In both, the cloud is near-white (brighter than the sunlit walls), built from equal round lobes with a crisp scalloped outline, and has a flat ragged line where it meets the floor. The lit side and the shaded side barely differ. It takes no warm or cool tint from the map (sandstone sun vs tunnel shade). In the dark Lower Tunnel it glows light grey (tun_t1.png). CS2 smoke (t4_017/t4_030/t4_009) is exposure-matched to the scene: dusty beige in sun and blue-grey in shade, with strong self-shadow. Its edges are broken and wispy and it feathers into the ground. To fix: cap the albedo or exposure well below the sunlit walls; take the ambient and sun colour from the local light probe; add a much stronger self-shadow gradient; make the lobes non-uniform and break them up; feather the floor contact.
other_gaps: Close-range and inside rendering has artifacts and is very expensive. In Lower Tunnel (cam -37,28 -> smoke -39,17, t=1 s) the cloud is a flat wall with vertical seam bands and dark blotchy smudges. Render cost: with swiftshader at 960x540 a frame takes 4-5 s with no smoke and 6 s with a smoke 13 m away. It takes 20.7 s at 7 m and 62.6 s at 3.5 m from the smoke. That is about 4x and 15x, purely from fill or overdraw. Two 1280x720 screenshots at 3 m timed out after 240 s. Expect GPU frame drops when a player stands at or inside a smoke, which is the most common place to be in a smoke fight.

Bot strobes flash their own team as often as the enemy. In bot-lab, seed 11, 5 rounds, 9000 credits (tools/utility_bot_flash.mjs 11 5 v): 31 throws (11 haze, 14 strobe, 6 pulse). Strobes caused 3 enemy blinds >=0.5 and 3 friendly blinds >=0.5. Vesper alone team-flashed the human 'You' at 0.93, Quill at 0.51 and Halo9 at 0.78. 6 of 14 strobes blinded nobody. EMBER threw 11 strobes and TIDE threw 3.

The aim preview is still wrong for jump-throws. Standing, crouching and running-while-held throws match exactly or within 0.25 m. Repro for the jump case: place(0,0,20, yaw 0, pitch -0.35), slot4, jump, press LMB 0.12 s later, release 0.25 s later. A Pulse was predicted to pop at z=0.33 but popped at z=-5.93 (6.3 m off). A Haze landed 0.5-1.0 m off and a Strobe at (38,30, pitch -0.3) landed 2.3 m off. Jump-throws are the standard lineup technique.
The smoke blooms almost instantly. It is a full dome by 0.3-0.5 s (hz_t0p3, lo_hub_t0p5), with no visible roll-out from the canister. In CS2 the smoke billows out over about 1 s.

Pulse ground dust is a vision blocker that only humans see. At 0.7 s after a pop 6 m away (pulse2_t0p7) a beige haze covers most of the screen, but blocksLine and opticalDepth only read Haze, so bots see through it.

The bullet hole is a pinhole that refills fast. One tap at 20 m opens a hole about 15 px wide (LOS clear and box visible, consistent). By 0.35 s it is blocked again (od 0.86). In CS2 bullet holes stay readable for longer.
bugs: Jump-throw preview mismatch: Pulse predicted pop at (0,0.07,0.33), actual pop at (0,0.07,-5.93). Repro in other_gaps[2].
Bots team-flash the human player: Vesper's strobe blinded 'You' at 0.93 (seed 11, bot-lab).
strengths: Preview is now exact for standing, crouched, wall-bank and run-held throws (0.00-0.27 m error).
Strobe peaks at pure white, holds about 1.8 s at 6 m facing the pop, then fades through a blurred frozen afterimage that feels like CS2.
Punch-through on screen matches LOS. One bullet opens a hole where blocksLine is false and the box is visible (vis 224 vs 0), and both close again together.
Smoke LOS is well behaved across a lateral sweep, and the flood fill confines to corridors with no leaks through walls.
Pulse looks good: hex dome, expanding ring, sparks and debris, clipped by walls, with sensible damage falloff (11 dmg at 5 m, 4 at 6 m).
No console errors from the game across about 10 sessions. Draw calls stay at about 83 with a smoke live.
